title: Epimorphic sheafified arrow families have genuine covering refinements
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in a universe containing its objects, morphisms and indexing sets [def-weil-size-convention], and take sheaves and presheaves of sets in that universe. For every $T\in\mathcal C$ put $h_T(V)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(V,T)$, $H_T=h_T^\#$, and let $\eta_T:h_T\to H_T$ be the sheafification unit [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Let $U\in\mathcal C$, let $I$ be a set, and let $(a_i:U_i\to U)_{i\in I}$ be any family of morphisms, not assumed to be a covering. Suppose the induced morphism $\coprod_{i\in I}H_{U_i}\to H_U$ from the coproduct in sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] is an epimorphism, meaning that for every sheaf $G$ and morphisms $f,g:H_U\to G$, equality of their composites with this coproduct morphism implies $f=g$. Then there exist a covering family $(v_b:V_b\to U)_{b\in B}$, a function $\alpha:B\to I$, and morphisms $g_b:V_b\to U_{\alpha(b)}$ satisfying $a_{\alpha(b)}\circ g_b=v_b$ for every $b\in B$. Thus the original arrow family has a covering refinement whose triangles commute in $\mathcal C$, without assuming the site is subcanonical.

source.place: Tag 0D06, lemma-quasi-compact, reverse proof after the finite epimorphic subfamily is selected: local representatives followed by local equality; no finiteness hypothesis is needed for this subargument.

proof.text: Let L be presheafToSheaf and let f be Sigma.desc of the presheaf maps h(a_i). Mathlib sigmaComparison_map_desc identifies the given epi with sigmaComparison L (h(U_i)) followed by L.map f. Hence L.map f is epi by cancellation. Mathlib Sheaf.isLocallySurjective_iff_epi and Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_presheafToSheaf_map_iff imply that f is locally surjective. For the common value universe, obtain WEqualsLocallyBijective by transporting along the equivalence with the small model of C (Mathlib WEqualsLocallyBijective.ofEssentiallySmall).
Apply Mathlib GrothendieckTopology.ofArrows_mem_iff_isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_uliftYoneda_map to deduce that the sieve generated by the original arrows is covering for J.toGrothendieck.

Extract a covering presieve R of J inside that covering sieve by induction on Precoverage.Saturate. A generating cover uses itself; the maximal sieve contains the singleton identity cover. For a pullback, index a cover R by all pairs (V,f) with f in R, apply the covering-pullback axiom of the site, and use the pullback square equation to place the new covering inside the pulled-back sieve. For transitivity, choose a covering presieve in each covering pullback over each distinct arrow of a covering presieve R, and apply the bind-composition axiom. Every composite lies in the desired sieve by its chosen local refinement. This uses only covering pullbacks, not pullbacks of arbitrary arrows, and no closure under independently repeated covering presentations.

source.place: Tag 00VH, definition-site, covering composition and covering pullbacks; induction on Mathlib Precoverage.Saturate

proof.text: Index the arrows of R by B = ULift of the dependent sum of objects V and arrows b:V to U belonging to R. Thus B lives in the common universe and Presieve.ofArrows V b is exactly R. Each b belongs to the sieve generated by the original family, so it factors as g followed by one a_i. Choose that label and factor for each b; these choices give alpha and g and the required strict triangle equations. Empty covers and empty I need no separate nonemptiness assumption.
